gold.title: Temporal/comparative naming: formatBytesEnhanced names the edit, not the behavior
gold.description: "Enhanced" relative to what? The name records that this function came after formatBytes, not what it does. Fold the negative-value handling into formatBytes or name the function for its behavior.

candidate.title: formatBytesEnhanced is a comparative-named parallel variant with silently different behavior
candidate.description: Two exported byte formatters differ only by Enhanced suffix; they disagree on negatives (formatBytes(-2048)→−2048.0 B vs formatBytesEnhanced(-2048)→−2.0 KB). formatBytesEnhanced has one consumer and delegates entirely to formatBytes; formatBytes has no external callers.

gold.title: Changelog-style comment records edit history in code
gold.description: "// Fixed bug where negative values were not handled" is commit-message content; in the file it goes stale the moment the code changes again. Git history already records it.

candidate.title: Comments on formatBytesEnhanced restate code or narrate history
candidate.description: Two comments (lines 13, 15) either restate what the signature shows or recite changelog text. Both will go stale on any change to the function.
